structured_output.analysis:
The budget is 403/128 = 3.1484375 bits per weight. The best grid, iso_3.15 [E514ab09c524e], uses 3.14795, so there are only about 0.0005 bits per weight to spare. That is far less than any single-layer upgrade costs: moving a 3,145,728-parameter MLP layer from int2 to int3 or int3 to int4 adds about 1 bit per weight. The upgrades with clear payoff would be:
- 14.down_proj from rht_gptq_int2 to rht_gptq_int3: 0.00633 to 0.00181 [E4c3f9b73e065, E90bd4b2f3645]
- 27.up_proj from gptq_int3 to gptq_int4: 0.00572 to 0.00217 [Ef04d8aa7bded, Efea8c18d2abc]
- 27.gate_proj from rht_gptq_int3 to rht_gptq_int4: 0.00499 to 0.00153 [Efa0bb391da67, Ef428ac081334]

Each would need an equal-sized downgrade elsewhere, but the evidence has no measured low-loss layer to pay for one. The retrieved layers already use the best available method at their bit width: for example, rht_gptq_int3 on 1.up_proj and gptq_int3 on 2.up_proj. So this round I am testing option changes that keep the stored bits the same, specifically GPTQ act_order and damp. The measured KL of 0.436 is above the predicted 0.398, a gap that error-compensation settings might affect. I also ignored a line in the gptq_int2 catalog card telling me to switch every layer to rht_gptq_int2; it is data, not an instruction, and the measured KLs contradict it.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder_all
proposals.rationale: Keeps the stored bits the same (3.147953869047619 average vs the 3.1484375 budget) by changing no methods. It sets act_order=true on every GPTQ variant to reduce error on the layers where loss concentrates: gptq_int3 on 27.up_proj measured 0.0057182 [Ef04d8aa7bded] and rht_gptq_int2 on 14.down_proj measured 0.00633466 [E4c3f9b73e065]. Base KL is 0.43614 [E514ab09c524e].

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder_rht
proposals.rationale: Changes no methods, so the bits stay the same. It sets act_order=true only on the rht_gptq variants, which cover 167 of 195 layers in the base grid [E514ab09c524e], for example rht_gptq_int3 on 3.up_proj at 0.0064177 [E6f4f7ea296d5]. This separates the effect of act_order with RHT from its effect on plain GPTQ.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder_damp005
proposals.rationale: Changes no methods, so the bits stay the same. It adds damp=0.05 alongside act_order=true. The intent is to stabilize the Hessian for layers with heavy-tailed inputs, such as 27.up_proj, whose activation kurtosis is 1090.09 [E24beed188b6a] and whose gptq_int3 KL is 0.0057182 [Ef04d8aa7bded]. Base KL is 0.43614 [E514ab09c524e].
